name: Payment Handler API
plain: Lets a payment app run inside the browser as a payment option.
meaning: Lets a wallet website register as a payment method; the site sees only the payment response.

access.prompt_ui: Payment sheet lists the registered handler after install
access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: Lets a payment app run inside the browser as a payment option.

limits.headline: Can offer its own pay option in the browser's payment sheet, once you install it
limits.user_action: You pick that payment app in the browser's payment sheet, after it was added.
can: Show up as a payment choice in the browser pay sheet
Open its own window to take payment details
Send the store an approval after you pay
cannot: Take money without you picking it
Work in Firefox or Safari, including on iPhone
See other payment apps you use
limits.reach_label: One payment, once you pick it
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge support it. Firefox and Safari do not.

story.what_it_is: A payment app can run inside the browser as a way to pay.

marketing.name: Web based payment apps
marketing.pitch: web.dev explains that Payment Handler lets a web based payment app show up in the browser pay sheet.

story.for_you: At checkout the browser pay sheet may list a payment app you installed from a website, like a bank or wallet app.
story.for_makers: Banks and wallets can offer their payment method without a native app. Merchants just ask for the payment method and the browser connects them.

use_cases.example: A bank registers its own payment app so customers pay with it at any merchant.
A digital wallet offers its balance as a payment choice.
A shop accepts any installed payment app without special integrations.
A web game sells in game currency using a wallet balance.
A booking site lets you pay with a loyalty points wallet.
A bank checks you in its own app before approving, so card theft is harder.

technical_bounds: Handler must be a service worker with HTTPS
